title: Evidence-to-Impact Accelerator
tagline: Combining research, incubation, policy translation, and scale into one closed-loop 10-stage engine.
description: Our premier flagship initiative. Rather than operating disconnected research, incubation, and training schemes, the Evidence-to-Impact Accelerator takes high-potential youth innovators through our 10-stage journey: Discover → Diagnose → Research → Design → Prototype → Policy → Finance → Implement → Measure → Scale.
eligibility: African young innovators, researchers, and changemakers aged 18–35
Demonstrated community problem statement backed by initial grassroots observation
Commitment to participatory research, prototyping, and policy dialogue
Cross-disciplinary teams combining technical, research, and civic leadership

howToParticipate.title: Community Discovery Submission
howToParticipate.description: Submit a problem dossier based on grassroots observation and community lived experience.

howToParticipate.title: Systems Diagnosis & Bootcamp
howToParticipate.description: Selected teams conduct root-cause political-economy analysis and evidence generation.

howToParticipate.title: Human-Centered Co-Design & Prototyping
howToParticipate.description: Build and field-test physical or digital prototypes directly with citizen end-users.

howToParticipate.title: Policy, Finance & Continental Scale
howToParticipate.description: Formulate statutory policy recommendations and pitch to capital syndicates at Demo Day.

curriculumHighlights: Policy Drafting, Regulatory Sandboxes & Investor Due Diligence
outcomes: 91% 2-year survival rate for incubated solutions with $6.4M+ in follow-on capital mobilized.

title: Policy Innovation Challenge
tagline: Our most unique product: designing evidence-based policy solutions to Africa's most pressing challenges.
description: Instead of asking 'What business would you like to start?', we ask: 'What is one of Africa's most pressing problems, and what evidence-based solution can you design?' Young teams work on real policy bottlenecks across youth employment, digital transformation, AI, agriculture, climate, and regional integration, concluding at Policy Innovation Demo Day.
eligibility: Youth researchers, advocates, technologists, and public policy graduates aged 20–32
Focus on real-world policy friction in key thematic sectors (AI, Climate, Jobs, Health)
Willingness to engage directly with parliamentary committees and ministries
Ability to formulate both policy memos and functional prototypes

howToParticipate.title: Challenge Brief
howToParticipate.description: Choose a core thematic problem and submit a 750-word evidence-backed diagnosis.

howToParticipate.title: Diagnosis & Policy Proposal
howToParticipate.description: Work with AfriYouth econometricians and legal mentors to draft statutory reforms.

howToParticipate.title: Prototype Development
howToParticipate.description: Build an implementation mechanism, regulatory sandbox model, or civic tool.

howToParticipate.title: Policy Innovation Demo Day
howToParticipate.description: Present policy pitches before ministerial panels, regional economic communities, and funders.

curriculumHighlights: Policy Analysis, Statutory Design & Regulatory Review
outcomes: 38 legislative interventions influenced across municipal, national, and AU levels.

title: African Youth Policy & Futures Fellowship
tagline: Training the next generation of African technocrats, policy architects, and strategic futurists.
description: A 9-month immersive fellowship connecting emerging researchers with African Union, regional economic community, and municipal policy advisors. Fellows translate field data into actionable legislative frameworks and author contributions to the Africa 2050 Futures Series.
eligibility: Aged 21–32 residing in Africa or of the African diaspora committed to return
Background in public policy, economics, law, sociology, data science, or STEM
Evidence of prior community research, publication, or civic engagement
Commitment of 15 hours/week for synchronous sessions and fieldwork

howToParticipate.title: Online Application
howToParticipate.description: Submit CV, academic credentials, and policy statement addressing an African socio-economic challenge.

howToParticipate.title: Futures Challenge Brief
howToParticipate.description: Complete a diagnostic policy brief analyzing 2030/2050 horizon trends.

howToParticipate.title: Panel Interview
howToParticipate.description: Meet with AfriYouth senior faculty and institutional partner representatives.

howToParticipate.title: Onboarding & Placement
howToParticipate.description: Commence induction in Kigali and receive assignment to an institutional policy desk.

outcomes: 86% of alumni now advising ministries, international NGOs, or multilateral agencies across 22 African nations.

title: AfriYouth Innovation Accelerator
tagline: De-risking and scaling youth-led social and technological enterprises across African markets.
description: Our signature venture accelerator operating on our proven model: Incubation → Acceleration → Demo Day. We provide early-stage African founders with seed capital, technical mentorship, HCD validation, and investor readiness.
eligibility: Founding team majority aged 18–35 with African nationality
Functional prototype or MVP addressing one of the Sustainable Development Goals
Focus areas: AgriTech, HealthTech, Climate Resilience, EdTech, or GovTech
Commitment to job creation, dignified employment, and community impact

howToParticipate.title: Venture Dossier
howToParticipate.description: Submit pitch deck, operational metrics, demo video, and theory of change.

howToParticipate.title: Technical Review
howToParticipate.description: AfriYouth venture team conducts product audit, community impact review, and code inspection.

howToParticipate.title: Pitch Day Selection
howToParticipate.description: Top 25 ventures pitch before investment committee and partner impact funds.

howToParticipate.title: Accelerator Deployment
howToParticipate.description: Catalytic funding disbursed with access to prototyping labs, mentors, and Demo Day.

curriculumHighlights: Human-Centered Design Sprints for Low-Bandwidth Environments
Investor Readiness, Financial Modeling & Demo Day Pitching
outcomes: $4.2M follow-on funding raised by cohort companies; 180,000+ citizens served.

title: Employability Bootcamp & University Programme
tagline: Moving African youth from Education → Employability → Employment → Career Progression.
description: A practical workforce transition platform featuring our mandatory experiential learning model: 'Learn → Practice → Apply → Receive feedback → Improve → Demonstrate'. Participants engage in complete real-world employability simulations.
eligibility: African university students in final year or recent graduates (0–3 years post-graduation)
Commitment to complete mandatory experiential simulations and portfolio development
Access to basic internet and device for simulation software and assessments

howToParticipate.title: Registration & Baseline
howToParticipate.description: Complete diagnostic professional competency assessment.

howToParticipate.title: Practical Training
howToParticipate.description: Master CV customization, cover letters, ATS optimization, and LinkedIn branding.

howToParticipate.title: Employability Simulation
howToParticipate.description: Execute fictional vacancy analysis, psychometric tests, and mock case interviews.

howToParticipate.title: Portfolio & Placement
howToParticipate.description: Finalize verified portfolio and connect to regional employer partner network.

curriculumHighlights: Job Searching Strategies & Customized Application Portfolios
Interview Readiness, Case Studies & Salary Negotiation
outcomes: 78% transition into verified formal employment or funded ventures within 6 months.

title: Professional Development Academy
tagline: Practical, evidence-based, outcome-oriented leadership and executive capability building.
description: Moving beyond traditional certificate-based seminars, our academy deploys: Professional Competency Assessment → Practical Training → Real-World Challenge → Feedback → Professional Portfolio.
eligibility: Early to mid-career professionals working in public service, social enterprise, or civil society
Desire to build verified competencies in AI skills, systems thinking, and impact M&E
Organizational sponsorship or independent commitment

howToParticipate.title: Competency Assessment
howToParticipate.description: Evaluate current capabilities across 6 core institutional leadership pillars.

howToParticipate.title: Skill Labs
howToParticipate.description: Engage in masterclasses on AI literacy, systems problem solving, and M&E.

howToParticipate.title: Real-World Challenge
howToParticipate.description: Tackle an authentic organizational bottleneck with peer team and expert faculty.

howToParticipate.title: Portfolio Defense
howToParticipate.description: Present verified strategic deliverable to earn executive credentials.

curriculumHighlights: Digital Productivity, AI Literacy & Responsible AI Use
outcomes: Over 1,200 professionals certified across 14 African nations.
